title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 79 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 467–469 (Night 79, continuing directly from nights-78), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 79 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The vizier Dandān, telling Ḍawʾ al-Makān how his father died, reports how King ʿUmar asked the five learned slave-girls for something from the reports of past peoples. The first girl’s speech gives counsel on refinement, on choosing and keeping a friend, and on the manners of judges, ending with sayings of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Alexander; the second girl steps forward as dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ فَنَظَرَ الْمَرْحُومُ وَالِدُكَ إِلَى الْجَوَارِي فَسَرَّتْهُ رُؤْيَتُهُنَّ وَقَالَ لَهُنَّ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْكُنَّ تُسْمِعُنِي شَيْأً مِمَّا تَعْرِفُهُ مِنْ أَخْبَارِ النَّاسِ الْمَاضِينَ وَالْأُمَمِ السَّابِقِينَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni fa-naẓara al-marḥūmu wālidaka ilā al-jawārī fa-sarrathu ruʾyatuhunna wa-qāla lahunna kullu wāḥidatin minkunna tusmiʿunī shayʾan mimmā taʿrifuhu min akhbāri al-nāsi al-māḍīna wa-al-umami al-sābiqīna
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to the king Ḍawʾ al-Makān: The late-mercied one, your father, looked at the slave-girls, and their sight pleased him, and he said to them: Each one of you shall let me hear something of what she knows of the reports of the people, the passing-ones, and the nations, the preceding-ones.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to King Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Your late father looked upon the slave-girls and was pleased at the sight of them, and he said to them: Let each of you tell me something of what she knows of the reports of the peoples and nations of the past.
sentences.n: The print has رؤبتهن, a misprint for رؤيتهن, corrected here. The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words. شيأ is the edition’s spelling of شيئاً.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddamat wāḥidatun minhunna wa-qabbalati al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And one of them stepped forward and kissed the earth between his two hands,
sentences.i: One of them stepped forward and kissed the ground before him,

sentences.t: وَقَالَتِ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ يَنْبَغِي لِذِي الْأَدَبِ أَنْ يَجْتَنِبَ الْفُضُولَ وَيَتَحَلَّي بِالْفَضَائِلِ وَأَنْ يُؤَدِّى الْفَرَائِضَ وَيَجْتَنِبَ الْكَبَائِرَ وَيُلَازِمَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مُلَازَمَةَ مَنْ لَوْ أُفْرِدَ عَنْهُ لَهَلَكَ وَأَسَاسُ الْأَدَبِ مَكَارِمُ الْأَخْلَاقِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālati iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu yanbaghī li-dhī al-adabi an yajtaniba al-fuḍūla wa-yataḥalla bi-al-faḍāʾili wa-an yuʾaddiya al-farāʾiḍa wa-yajtaniba al-kabāʾira wa-yulāzima ʿalā dhālika mulāzamata man law ufrida ʿanhu la-halaka wa-asāsu al-adabi makārimu al-akhlāqi
sentences.l: And she said: Know, O king, that it is fitting for the possessor-of-refinement that he avoid the superfluities and adorn himself with the virtues, and that he perform the obligations and avoid the great sins, and cleave to that with the cleaving of one who, were he separated from it, would perish; and the foundation of refinement is the noble-qualities of the characters.
sentences.i: And she said: Know, O king, that a man of refinement ought to shun idle excess and adorn himself with virtues, to perform the obligatory duties and avoid the great sins, and to hold to this as one holds to what he would perish without; for the foundation of refinement is nobility of character.
sentences.n: ويتحلي and تعالي (below) are written with a final yā where Classical spelling has alif maqṣūra; the edition does this often and it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ مُعْظَمَ أَسْبَابِ الْمَعِيشَةِ طَلَبُ الْحَيَاةِ وَالْقَصْدُ مِنَ الْحَيَاةِ عِبَادَةُ اللَّهِ فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُحَسِّنَ خُلُقَكَ مَعَ النَّاسِ وَأَنْ لَا تَعْدِلَ عَنْ تِلْكَ السُّنَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna muʿẓama asbābi al-maʿīshati ṭalabu al-ḥayāti wa-al-qaṣdu mina al-ḥayāti ʿibādatu allāhi fa-yanbaghī an tuḥassina khuluqaka maʿa al-nāsi wa-an lā taʿdila ʿan tilka al-sunnati
sentences.l: And know that the greater-part of the causes of livelihood is the seeking of life, and the aim from life is the worship of God; so it is fitting that you make good your character with the people, and that you not swerve from that way.
sentences.i: And know that most of the means of livelihood amount to the pursuit of life, while the aim of life is the worship of God; so you should perfect your character toward people and not swerve from that path.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ أَعْظَمَ النَّاسِ خَطَراً أَحْوَجُهُمْ إِلَى التَّدْبِيرِ وَالْمُلُوكُ أَحْوَجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ السُّوقَةِ لِأَنَّ السُّوقَةَ قَدْ تَفِيضُ فِى الْأُمُورِ مِنْ غَيْرِ نَظَرٍ فِى الْعَاقِبَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna aʿẓama al-nāsi khaṭaran aḥwajuhum ilā al-tadbīri wa-al-mulūku aḥwaju ilayhi mina al-sūqati li-anna al-sūqata qad tafīḍu fī al-umūri min ghayri naẓarin fī al-ʿāqibati
sentences.l: For the greatest of the people in rank is the most needy of them for planning, and the kings are more needy of it than the common-folk, because the common-folk may well plunge into affairs without a looking at the outcome,
sentences.i: For the greater a man’s standing, the more he needs forethought, and kings need it more than commoners, since commoners may well plunge into affairs without a glance at the outcome,

sentences.t: وَأَنْ نَبْذُلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ نَفْسَكَ وَمَالَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-an nabdhula fī sabīli allāhi nafsaka wa-mālaka
sentences.l: and that we spend, in the way of God, your self and your wealth.
sentences.i: and that you spend yourself and your wealth in the way of God.
sentences.n: The print has نبذل (“we spend”) beside نفسك (“your self”); the sense wants تبذل, “you spend”, and the idiomatic line follows that. Vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْعَدُوَّ خَصْمٌ تَخْصِمُهُ وَتَعْرِفُهُ بِالْحُجَّةِ وَتَحْتَرِزُ مِنْهُ وَأَمَّا الصَّدِيقُ فَلَيْسَ بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ قَاضٍ يَحْكُمُ غَيْرُ حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna al-ʿaduwwa khaṣmun takhṣimuhu wa-taʿrifuhu bi-al-ḥujjati wa-taḥtarizu minhu wa-ammā al-ṣadīqu fa-laysa baynaka wa-baynahu qāḍin yaḥkumu ghayru ḥusni al-khuluqi
sentences.l: And know that the enemy is an adversary whom you oppose and know by the proof, and guard against; but as for the friend, there is not between you and him a judge who rules other than good character.
sentences.i: And know that an enemy is an adversary you can contend with, one you know by his arguments and guard against; but between you and a friend there is no judge to rule but good character.

sentences.t: فَاخْتَرْ صَدِيقَكَ لِنَفْسِكَ بَعْدَ اخْتِارِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ikhtar ṣadīqaka li-nafsika baʿda ikhtārihi
sentences.l: So choose your friend for yourself after his …
sentences.i: So choose your friend for yourself, and only after you have tried him.
sentences.n: اختاره looks like a letter has dropped out: اختياره (“choosing him”) or اختباره (“testing him”). It is vocalised as printed, and the idiomatic line follows the second reading.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ إِخْوَانِ الْآخِرَةِ فَلْيَكُنْ مُحَافِظاً عَلَى اتِّبَاعِ ظَاهِرِ الشَّرْعِ عَارِفاً بِبَاطِنِهِ عَلَى حَسَبِ الْإِمْكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-in kāna min ikhwāni al-ākhirati fa-li-yakun muḥāfiẓan ʿalā ittibāʿi ẓāhiri al-sharʿi ʿārifan bi-bāṭinihi ʿalā ḥasabi al-imkāni
sentences.l: So if he is of the brothers of the hereafter, let him be a guardian over the following of the outward of the law, knowing its inward according to what is possible.
sentences.i: If he is to be a brother for the hereafter, let him be careful to follow the outward letter of the law and know its inner meaning as far as he can.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ إِخْوَانِ الدُّنْيَا فَلْيَكُنْ حُرّاً صَادِقاً لَيْسَ بِجَاهِلٍ وَلَاشَرِيرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-in kāna min ikhwāni al-dunyā fa-li-yakun ḥurran ṣādiqan laysa bi-jāhilin wa-lā-sharīrin
sentences.l: And if he is of the brothers of the world, let him be free, truthful, not an ignorant one nor a wicked one;
sentences.i: And if he is to be a brother for this world, let him be a free and truthful man, neither ignorant nor wicked;

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْجَاهِلَ أَهْلٌ لِأَنْ يَقْرُبَ مِنْهُ أَبَوَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-jāhila ahlun li-an yaqruba minhu abawāhu
sentences.l: for the ignorant one is worthy that his two parents draw near him,
sentences.i: for the ignorant man deserves that even his own parents should approach him …
sentences.n: This clause is obscure and may be corrupt; يقرب (“draw near”) may stand for يهرب, “flee”, which would give “deserves that even his parents flee from him”. It is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: وَالْكَاذِبُ لَايَكُونُ صَدِيقاً لِأَنَّ الصَّدِيقَ مَأْخُوذٌ مِنَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي يَكُونُ نَاشِأً عَنْ صَمِيمِ الْقَلْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-kādhibu lā-yakūnu ṣadīqan li-anna al-ṣadīqa maʾkhūdhun mina al-ṣidqi alladhī yakūnu nāshiʾan ʿan ṣamīmi al-qalbi
sentences.l: and the liar is not a friend, because the friend is taken from truthfulness, which is arising from the core of the heart;
sentences.i: and a liar cannot be a friend, because the word for friend is taken from truthfulness, which springs from the very core of the heart.
sentences.n: The play is on ṣadīq (“friend”) and ṣidq (“truthfulness”), which share their root.

sentences.t: فَكَيْفَ بِهِ إِذَا أَظْهَرَ الْكَذِبَ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-kayfa bihi idhā aẓhara al-kadhiba ʿalā al-lisāni
sentences.l: So how is it with him when he shows lying upon the tongue?
sentences.i: How then can it be with a man who lets lies show on his tongue?

sentences.t: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اتِّبَاعَ الشَّرْعِ يَنْفَعُ صَاحِبَهُ فَأَحْبِبْ أَخَاكَ إِذَا كَانَ بِهَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ وَلَا تَقْطَعْهُ وَإِنْ ظَهَرَلَكَ مِنْهُ مَا تَكْرَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿlam anna ittibāʿa al-sharʿi yanfaʿu ṣāḥibahu fa-aḥbib akhāka idhā kāna bi-hādhihi al-ṣifati wa-lā taqṭaʿhu wa-in ẓahara-laka minhu mā takrahu
sentences.l: And know that the following of the law benefits its possessor; so love your brother when he is of this description, and do not cut him off, even if there appears to you from him what you dislike,
sentences.i: And know that following the law benefits the one who follows it. So love your brother when he is of this kind, and do not cast him off, even if something you dislike appears in him;

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ كَالْمَرْأَةِ يُمْكِنُ طَلَاقُهَا وَمُرَاجَعَتُهَا بَلْ قَلْبُهُ كَالزُّجَاجِ إِذَا انْصَدَعَ لَايَنْجَبِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu laysa ka-al-marʾati yumkinu ṭalāquhā wa-murājaʿatuhā bal qalbuhu ka-al-zujāji idhā inṣadaʿa lā-yanjabiru
sentences.l: for he is not like the woman, whose divorce and taking-back is possible; rather his heart is like glass: when it cracks, it is not mended.
sentences.i: for he is not like a wife, whom one may divorce and take back; his heart is like glass, which once cracked cannot be mended.
sentences.n: ك in كَالْمَرْأَةِ is the preposition “like”.

sentences.t: وَلِلَّهِ دَرُّالْقَائِ — لِ
sentences.tr: wa-li-llāhi darru-al-qāʾi — li
sentences.l: And to God belongs the milk of the sa-… — -yer:
sentences.i: And how well the poet said:
sentences.n: The word القائل (“the sayer”) is broken across the line in the print, with a dash and its last letter standing apart. وللّه درّ is an exclamation of praise (“God’s be his milk!”, i.e. “how splendid is …”).

sentences.t:
اِحْرِصْ عَلَى فَرْطِ الْقُلُوبِ مِنَ الْاَذَى * فَرُجُوعُهَا بَعْدَ التَّنَا فُرِ يَعْسُرُ
اِنَّ الْقُلُوبَ اِذَا تَنَا فَرُودُّ هَا * مِثْلُ الزَّجَاجَةِ كَسْرُهَا لَا يُجْبَرُ
sentences.tr:
iḥriṣ ʿalā farṭi al-qulūbi mina al-adhā * fa-rujūʿuhā baʿda al-tanāfuri yaʿsuru
inna al-qulūba idhā tanāfarū waddu-hā * mithlu al-zujājati kasruhā lā yujbaru
sentences.l:
Be careful of the excess of hearts against hurt, * for their returning after the shunning is hard.
Indeed hearts, when they shun, and their love * is like the glass: its breaking is not mended.
sentences.i:
Take care to guard hearts from harm, for once they have turned away it is hard to win them back.
Hearts that have grown estranged, and their love with them, are like glass: what is broken is not mended.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all, including the spaces it prints inside تَنَا فُرِ and تَنَا فَرُودُّ هَا. The second line is corrupt-looking (تنافروِدّها, “they shun, and their love”), and فرط in the first line is obscure; both are translated tentatively.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ فِي آخِرِ كَلَامِهَا وَهِيَ تُشِيرُ إِلَيْنَا إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْعُقُولِ قَالُوا
sentences.tr: thumma qālati al-jāriyatu fī ākhiri kalāmihā wa-hiya tushīru ilaynā inna aṣḥāba al-ʿuqūli qālū
sentences.l: Then the girl said at the end of her speech, while she was pointing to us: Indeed the possessors of minds have said:
sentences.i: Then the girl said, as she came to the end of her speech and made a sign toward us: The people of understanding have said:

sentences.t: خَيْرُ الْإِخْوَانِ أَشَدُّهُمْ فِى النَّصِيحَةِ وَخَيْرُ الْأَعْمَالِ أَجْمَلُهَا عَاقِبَةً وَخَيْرُ الثَّنَاءِ مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَفْوَاهِ الرِّجَالِ
sentences.tr: khayru al-ikhwāni ashadduhum fī al-naṣīḥati wa-khayru al-aʿmāli ajmaluhā ʿāqibatan wa-khayru al-thanāʾi mā kāna ʿalā afwāhi al-rijāli
sentences.l: The best of the brothers is the strongest of them in counsel, and the best of the deeds is the fairest of them in outcome, and the best of the praise is what is upon the mouths of the men.
sentences.i: The best of brothers is the one most earnest in counsel; the best of deeds is the one with the fairest outcome; and the best of praise is what is on the lips of men.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ لَاينْبَغِي لِلْعَبْدِ أَنْ يَغْفُلَ عَنْ شُكْرِاللَّهِ خُصُوصاً عَلَى نِعْمَتَيْنِ الْعَافِيَةِ وَالْعَقْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla lā-yanbaghī li-al-ʿabdi an yaghfula ʿan shukri-allāhi khuṣūṣan ʿalā niʿmatayni al-ʿāfiyati wa-al-ʿaqli
sentences.l: And it has been said: It is not fitting for the servant that he be heedless of the thanks of God, especially for two blessings, health and the mind.
sentences.i: And it has been said: A servant of God ought never to forget to give thanks, especially for two blessings, health and reason.

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ مَنْ كَرُمَتْ عَلَيْهِ نَفْسُهُ هَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ شَهْوَتُهُ وَمَنْ عَظَّمَ صَغَائِرَ الْمَصَائِبِ ابْتِلَاءُ اللَّهِ بِكِبَارِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qīla man karumat ʿalayhi nafsuhu hānat ʿalayhi shahwatuhu wa-man ʿaẓẓama ṣaghāʾira al-maṣāʾibi ibtilāʾu allāhi bi-kibārihā
sentences.l: And it was said: He for whom his self is noble, his desire is easy for him; and he who magnifies the small of the misfortunes — the trial of God with the great ones of them.
sentences.i: And it was said: Whoever holds his own soul dear finds his appetite easy to master; and whoever makes much of small misfortunes, God afflicts him with great ones.
sentences.n: The print has ابتلاء (“the trial of”) where ابتلاه (“tried him”) is evidently meant, so that the clause reads “God tries him with their great ones”. It is vocalised as printed and the idiomatic line follows the sense.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ أَطَاعَ الْهَوَى ضَيَّعَ الْحُقُوقَ وَمَنْ أَطَاعَ الْوَاشِي ضَيَّعَ الصَّدِيقَ
sentences.tr: wa-man aṭāʿa al-hawā ḍayyaʿa al-ḥuqūqa wa-man aṭāʿa al-wāshī ḍayyaʿa al-ṣadīqa
sentences.l: And he who obeys desire loses the rights, and he who obeys the informer loses the friend.
sentences.i: Whoever obeys his passion neglects what is due, and whoever heeds the slanderer loses his friend.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ ظَنَّ بِكَ خَيْراً فَصَدِّقْ ظَنَّهُ بِكَ وَمَنْ بَالَغَ فِى الْخُصُومَةِ أَثِمَ
sentences.tr: wa-man ẓanna bika khayran fa-ṣaddiq ẓannahu bika wa-man bālagha fī al-khuṣūmati athima
sentences.l: And he who thinks good of you, then prove true his thinking of you; and he who goes to extremes in quarrelling sins.
sentences.i: If anyone thinks well of you, prove his opinion of you true; and whoever carries a quarrel to extremes commits sin.

sentences.t: وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْذَرِ الْحَيْفَ لَمْ يَأْ مَنِ السَّيْفَ
sentences.tr: wa-man lam yaḥdhari al-ḥayfa lam yaʾ manī al-sayfa
sentences.l: And he who does not beware injustice is not safe from the sword.
sentences.i: Whoever does not beware of wrongdoing will not be safe from the sword.
sentences.n: The print breaks يأمن into يأ من across a space; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَذْكُرُ لَكَ شَيْأً مِنْ آدَابِ الْقُضَاةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā adhkuru laka shayʾan min ādābi al-quḍāti
sentences.l: And behold, I mention to you something of the proprieties of the judges.
sentences.i: And now I shall tell you something of the manners proper to judges.

sentences.t: اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّهُ لَا يَنْفَعُ حُكْمٌ بِحَقٍّ إِلَّا بَعْدَ التَّثَبُّتِ
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku annahu lā yanfaʿu ḥukmun bi-ḥaqqin illā baʿda al-tathabbuti
sentences.l: Know, O king, that a judgment with truth does not profit except after verification.
sentences.i: Know, O king, that a ruling, even a just one, is of no use unless it comes after careful verification.

sentences.t: وَيَنْبَغِي لِلْقَاضِي أَنْ يَجْعَلَ النَّاسَ فِي مَنْزِلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ حَتَّى لَا يَطْمَعَ شَرِيفٌ فِى الْجَوْرِ وَلَا يَيْأَسَ ضَعِيفٌ مِنَ الْعَدْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-yanbaghī li-al-qāḍī an yajʿala al-nāsa fī manzilatin wāḥidatin ḥattā lā yaṭmaʿa sharīfun fī al-jawri wa-lā yayʾasa ḍaʿīfun mina al-ʿadli
sentences.l: And it is fitting for the judge that he put the people in one standing, so that a noble not covet injustice, nor a weak one despair of justice.
sentences.i: And a judge ought to treat all people alike, so that no nobleman hopes for favour in wrongdoing and no weak man despairs of justice.

sentences.t: وَيَنْبَغِي أَيْضاً أَنْ يَجْعَلَ الْبَيِّنَةَ عَلَى مَنْ ادَّعَى وَالْيَمِينَ عَلَى مَنْ أَنْكَرَ وَالصُّلْحُ جَائِزٌ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَّاصُلْحاً أَحَلَّ حَرَاماً أَوْ حَرَّمَ حَلَالاً
sentences.tr: wa-yanbaghī aydan an yajʿala al-bayyinata ʿalā man iddaʿā wa-al-yamīna ʿalā man ankara wa-al-ṣulḥu jāʾizun bayna al-muslimīna illā-ṣulḥan aḥalla ḥarāman aw ḥarrama ḥalālan
sentences.l: And it is fitting also that he put the proof upon him who claimed, and the oath upon him who denied; and settlement is permitted among the Muslims, except a settlement that made lawful a forbidden thing or made forbidden a lawful thing.
sentences.i: He should also lay the burden of proof on the claimant and the oath on the one who denies; and settlement between Muslims is permitted, unless it makes lawful what is forbidden or forbids what is lawful.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَشْكَلْتَ فِيهِ الْيَوْمَ فَرَاجِعْ فِيهِ عَقْلَكَ وَتَبَيَّنْ بِهِ رُشْدَكَ لِتَرْجِعَ فِيهِ إِلَى الْحَقِّ فَالْحَقُّ فَرْضٌ وَالرُّجُوعُ إِلَى الْحَقِّ خَيْرٌ مِنَ التَّمَادِي عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ashkalta fīhi al-yawma fa-rājiʿ fīhi ʿaqlaka wa-tabayyan bihi rushdaka li-tarjiʿa fīhi ilā al-ḥaqqi fa-al-ḥaqqu farḍun wa-al-rujūʿu ilā al-ḥaqqi khayrun mina al-tamādī ʿalā al-bāṭili
sentences.l: And what you made confusing in it today, consult your mind about it, and make clear by it your right-guidance, so that you return in it to the truth; for the truth is an obligation, and the returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood.
sentences.i: And if you went wrong in a matter today, review it with your reason and make your right course clear by it, so that you return to the truth; for the truth is an obligation, and returning to it is better than persisting in falsehood.
sentences.n: أشكلت is vocalised as a second-person verb (“you made confusing”); the clause is loose and the verb possibly misread, so the idiomatic line gives the sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اعْرِفِ الْأَمْثَالَ وَافْقَهِ الْمَقَالَ وَسَوِّبَيْنَ الْأَخْصَامِ فِى الْوُقُوفِ وَلْيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ عَلَى الْحَقِّ مَوْقُوفاً
sentences.tr: thumma iʿrifi al-amthāla wa-ifqahi al-maqāla wa-sawwi-bayna al-akhṣāmi fī al-wuqūfi wa-li-yakun naẓaruka ʿalā al-ḥaqqi mawqūfan
sentences.l: Then know the likenesses, and understand the speech, and make equal between the adversaries in the standing; and let your looking upon the truth be …
sentences.i: Then learn the precedents and grasp what is said, and treat the parties alike as they stand before you; and let your gaze rest steadily on the truth.
sentences.n: The print has موتوفا, a misprint for موقوفا, corrected here. “The standing” is the parties’ standing before the judge.

sentences.t: وَفَوِّضْ أَمْرَكَ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَاجْعَلِ الْبَيِّنَةَ عَلَى مَنْ ادَّعَى فَإِنْ حَضَرَتْ بَيِّنَتُهُ أَخَذْتَ لَهُ بِحَقِّهِ وَإِلَّاحَلِّفِ الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ وَهَذَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-fawwiḍ amraka ilā allāhi ʿazza wa-jalla wa-ijʿali al-bayyinata ʿalā man iddaʿā fa-in ḥaḍarat bayyinatuhu akhadhta lahu bi-ḥaqqihi wa-illā-ḥallifi al-muddaʿā ʿalayhi wa-hādhā ḥukmu allāhi
sentences.l: And commit your affair to God, mighty and majestic, and put the proof upon him who claimed; and if his proof is present, you take for him his right, and if not, make the one-claimed-against swear; and this is the judgment of God.
sentences.i: Entrust your affair to God, mighty and glorious, and lay the burden of proof on the claimant. If his proof is brought, award him his right; if not, make the defendant swear. This is the judgment of God.
sentences.n: The print joins وإلا to the verb (والاحلّف) and omits the final tā’; it is read as the imperative حَلِّفِ, “make swear”, answering أخذتَ before it.

sentences.t: وَاقْبَلْ شَهَادَةَ عُدُولِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَمَرَ الْحُكَّامَ أَنْ تَحْكُمَ بِالظَّاهِرِ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى السَّرَائِرَ
sentences.tr: wa-iqbal shahādata ʿudūli al-muslimīna baʿḍihim ʿalā baʿḍin fa-inna allāha taʿālā amara al-ḥukkāma an taḥkuma bi-al-ẓāhiri wa-huwa yatawallā al-sarāʾira
sentences.l: And accept the testimony of the upright of the Muslims, some of them against others; for God, exalted, has commanded the rulers to rule by the outward, and He takes charge of the secrets.
sentences.i: Accept the testimony of upright Muslims against one another; for God Most High has commanded rulers to judge by outward appearance, while He Himself deals with what is hidden.

sentences.t: وَيَجِبُ عَلَى الْقَاضِي أَنْ يَجْتَنِبَ الْقَضَاءَ عِنْدَ شِدَّةِ الْأَلَمِ وَالْجُوعِ وَأَنْ يَقْصِدَ بِقَضَائِهِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَي
sentences.tr: wa-yajibu ʿalā al-qāḍī an yajtaniba al-qaḍāʾa ʿinda shiddati al-alami wa-al-jūʿi wa-an yaqṣida bi-qaḍāʾihi bayna al-nāsi wajha allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And it is obligatory upon the judge that he avoid judging at the intensity of pain and hunger, and that he intend, by his judging between the people, the face of God, exalted.
sentences.i: A judge must avoid giving judgment in the grip of pain or hunger, and in judging between people he must seek the face of God Most High.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ مَنْ خَلُصَتْ نِيَّتُهُ وَأَصْلَحَ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ كَفَاهُ اللَّهُ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna man khaluṣat niyyatuhu wa-aṣlaḥa mā baynahu wa-bayna nafsihi kafāhu allāhu mā baynahu wa-bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: For he whose intention is pure, and who sets right what is between him and his self, God suffices him for what is between him and the people.
sentences.i: For if a man’s intention is pure and he sets right what lies between himself and his own soul, God will see to what lies between him and other people.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ ثَلَٰثٌ إِذَا كُنَّ فِي قَاضٍ كَانَ مُنْعَزِلاً إِذَا أَكْرَمَ اللِّئَامَ وَأَحَبَّ الْمَحَامِدَ وَكَرِهَ الْعَزْلَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-Zuhriyyu thalāthun idhā kunna fī qāḍin kāna munʿazilan idhā akrama al-liʾāma wa-aḥabba al-maḥāmida wa-kariha al-ʿazla
sentences.l: And al-Zuhrī said: Three, when they are in a judge, he is dismissed: when he honours the base, and loves praises, and dislikes dismissal.
sentences.i: And al-Zuhrī said: There are three things which, when they are found in a judge, mean that he is as good as dismissed: honouring the base, loving praise, and dreading dismissal.
sentences.n: ثلث is the edition’s defective spelling of ثلاث, “three”, and takes the dagger alif.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ عَزَلَ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ قَاضِياً فَقَالَ لَهُ لِمَ عَزَلْتَنِي فَقَالَ عُمَرُ قَدْ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكَ أَنَّ مَقَالَكَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ مَقَامِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ʿazala ʿumaru ibnu ʿabdi al-ʿazīzi qāḍiyan fa-qāla lahu lima ʿazaltanī fa-qāla ʿumaru qad balaghanī ʿanka anna maqālaka akbaru min maqāmika
sentences.l: And ʿUmar son of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz had dismissed a judge, and he said to him: Why did you dismiss me? And ʿUmar said: It has reached me about you that your speech is greater than your station.
sentences.i: Now ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz once dismissed a judge, who said to him: Why have you dismissed me? ʿUmar replied: It has reached me that your talk is greater than your standing.
sentences.n: The judge’s words are quoted as printed: he speaks of ʿUmar’s dismissing him (“you dismissed me”), as the sense requires.

sentences.t: وَحُكِيَ أَنَّ الْإِسْكَنْدَرَ قَالَ لِقَاضِيهِ إِنِّي وَلَّيْتُكَ مَنْزِلَةً وَاسْتَوْدَعْتُكَ فِيهَا رُوحِي وَعِرْضِي وَمُرُوءَتِي فَاحْفَظْ هَذِهِ الْمَنْزِلَةَ لِنَفْسِكَ وَعَقْلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥukiya anna al-iskandara qāla li-qāḍīhi innī wallaytuka manzilatan wa-istawdaʿtuka fīhā rūḥī wa-ʿirḍī wa-muruʾatī fa-iḥfaẓ hādhihi al-manzilata li-nafsika wa-ʿaqlika
sentences.l: And it is related that Alexander said to his judge: I have appointed you to a station, and entrusted you in it with my spirit and my honour and my manliness; so guard this station for your self and your mind.
sentences.i: It is told that Alexander said to his judge: I have set you in a station, and in it I have entrusted you with my life, my honour and my manhood; so guard this station for your own sake and for your reason’s.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِطَبَّاخِهِ إِنَّكَ مُسَلَّطٌ عَلَى جِسْمِي فَارْفُقْ بِنَفْسِكَ فِيهِ وَقَالَ لِكَاتِبِهِ إِنَّكَ مُتَصَرِّفٌ فِي عَقْلِي فَاحْفَظْنِي فِيمَا تَكْتُبُهُ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-ṭabbākhihi innaka musallaṭun ʿalā jismī fa-irfuq bi-nafsika fīhi wa-qāla li-kātibihi innaka mutaṣarrifun fī ʿaqlī fa-iḥfaẓnī fīmā taktubuhu ʿannī
sentences.l: And he said to his cook: You are given-power over my body, so be gentle with your self in it; and he said to his secretary: You are a disposer in my mind, so … me in what you write from me.
sentences.i: And he said to his cook: You have power over my body, so be gentle with yourself in it; and to his secretary: You are the manager of my mind, so keep me safe in what you write on my behalf.
sentences.n: The print has فاخفطني, a misprint for فاحفظني, corrected here.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَأَخَّرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ الْأُولَى وَتَقَدَّمَتِ الثَّانِيَةُ
sentences.tr: thumma taʾakhkharati al-jāriyatu al-ūlā wa-taqaddamati al-thāniyatu
sentences.l: Then the first girl drew back, and the second stepped forward.
sentences.i: Then the first girl drew back and the second stepped forward.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted tale unsaid.
